Package com.privatechain.spring

Class BlockchainAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
com.privatechain.spring.BlockchainAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration @EnableConfigurationProperties(BlockchainProperties.class) @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix="blockchain", name="enabled", havingValue="true", matchIfMissing=true) public class BlockchainAutoConfiguration extends Object
Spring Boot autoconfiguration for the private-blockchain library.

This class is the single assembly point for all blockchain Spring beans, mirroring the non-Spring assembly model in BlockchainConfig but adapting it to dependency injection (FR-CFG-01, FR-CFG-03).

Activation

Active by default. Disable completely with:


 blockchain:
   enabled: false

Zero-configuration start (AC-10)

No blockchain.* properties required. Defaults: ProofOfWorkEngine (difficulty 4) + InMemoryStorage.

Override points (T-072)

Every bean is guarded by @ConditionalOnMissingBean. Provide any of the following in your @Configuration to replace the default:

  • BlockchainNode — replaces the entire node
  • ConsensusEngine — replaces ProofOfWorkEngine
  • BlockchainStorage — replaces InMemoryStorage
  • BlockchainHealthIndicator — replaces the status bean

Multiple validators and listeners

All TransactionValidator and BlockchainEventListener beans are discovered and registered automatically in declaration order.

Node lifecycle

The BlockchainNode bean uses initMethod = "start" and destroyMethod = "stop". Spring calls start() after all beans are wired and stop() on context close.

Actuator integration

BlockchainHealthIndicator is a plain status-provider bean with no compile-time dependency on spring-boot-actuator. To wire it into the Actuator health endpoint, add this to your @Configuration:


 @Bean
 HealthIndicator blockchainHealth(BlockchainHealthIndicator indicator) {
     return () -> indicator.isUp()
         ? Health.up().withDetails(indicator.getDetails()).build()
         : Health.down().withDetails(indicator.getDetails()).build();
 }

  • Method Details

    • blockchainNode

      @Bean(initMethod="start", destroyMethod="stop") @ConditionalOnMissingBean public BlockchainNode blockchainNode(BlockchainProperties properties, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<ConsensusEngine> engineProvider, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<BlockchainStorage> storageProvider, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<TransactionValidator> validatorProvider, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<BlockchainEventListener> listenerProvider)
      Creates and wires the BlockchainNode bean from bound properties and any user-provided override beans (T-070, T-072).

      Dependency resolution order

      1. ConsensusEngine — user bean if present; else ProofOfWorkEngine with configured difficulty.
      2. BlockchainStorage — user bean if present; else InMemoryStorage (ephemeral, for dev/demo).
      3. TransactionValidator — all beans, chained in order (FR-TX-03).
      4. BlockchainEventListener — all beans, registered in order (FR-EVENT-02).

      The node is not started here. Spring calls start() via initMethod after all beans are fully wired.

      Parameters:
      properties - bound blockchain.* properties
      engineProvider - optional ConsensusEngine override
      storageProvider - optional BlockchainStorage override
      validatorProvider - zero or more TransactionValidator beans
      listenerProvider - zero or more BlockchainEventListener beans
      Returns:
      configured, not-yet-started BlockchainNode

    • blockchainHealthIndicator

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public BlockchainHealthIndicator blockchainHealthIndicator(BlockchainNode node)
      Creates the BlockchainHealthIndicator status bean.

      This is a plain POJO — it does not implement spring-boot-actuator's HealthIndicator interface, keeping this module free of a mandatory Actuator dependency. See BlockchainHealthIndicator for instructions on bridging it to Actuator's health endpoint (T-070).

      Guarded by @ConditionalOnMissingBean so applications can replace it without touching library sources (T-072).

      Parameters:
      node - the autoconfigured or user-provided BlockchainNode
      Returns:
      status provider for the running node
